name: discover-layer-compu-methods-full
description: The `compu_methods` layer's descriptor at `form: "full"` — the one form that carries the descriptor PROSE, asked for one layer at a time because the project-wide `full` discovery is REFUSED with `over-budget` on every project (`negative/discover-project-full-over-budget.json`), and the refusal's second step is exactly this request. Together the fifteen per-layer `full` vectors replay every layer, kind and field annotation the model contract ships, verbatim, which is where the shipped-prose oracle (`packages/tools/tests/test_model_contract_conformance.py`) rides: rewording an annotation in the contract is a protocol-output change, and this is the output it changes. Of this layer: the `compu_methods` layer contract `8.0.0` added for the computation method a type names by reference, stored in `data_types/compu_methods/`, with two kinds discriminated by `kind` -- `texttable`, whose `entries` are a member kind of their own, and `linear` -- an enumeration's, a value type's and a reference type's `compu_method_ref` naming a `texttable` and an application type's a `linear`.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` shape of a SWCraft project: fifteen scaffolded layers, `compu_methods` among them and empty in `data_types/compu_methods/`. Nothing about the response depends on which elements are in the layer: the inventory is derived from the model contract through the registry, not from the files.

layers.description: Computation methods, one file each under `data_types/compu_methods/`: how a stored value becomes the physical or the named one, an element a type names by reference. Two element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`texttable`, `linear`), plus one nested member kind (`table_entry`). An enumeration, a value type and a reference type name a `texttable` by their `compu_method_ref`, an application type names a `linear` by its own. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

element_kinds.description: A computation method of category `TEXTTABLE`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: a table of named values, one closed single-point `COMPU-SCALE` per entry, the shape an enumeration's own generated method has. An enumeration names one by its `compu_method_ref` in place of inline `literals`, and an implementation value or reference type by its `compu_method_ref`, which is the one way an implementation type states literals.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `texttable`.

fields.name: entries
fields.description: The table's named values, addressed by `name`, in the order they are emitted. Must not be empty: a `TEXTTABLE` holds one or more scales.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

element_kinds.description: A computation method of category `LINEAR`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: physical = stored × `factor` + `offset`, one `COMPU-SCALE` in the internal-to-physical direction, referring to the `unit` element it names. An application type names one by its `compu_method_ref`, in place of an inline `conversion`. It holds no scale label, which the standard makes not applicable for a `LINEAR` scale; the scale's limits are its optional `limits`.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `linear`.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: The name of the declared unit, an element of the `units` layer, the method refers to: a `LINEAR` computation method refers to a unit. Must not be blank.

fields.name: factor
fields.description: The multiplier applied to the stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

fields.name: offset
fields.description: The constant added after the multiplication. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

fields.name: limits
fields.description: The limits of the linear computation method's scale, on the stored side: the values the conversion is defined for, which is what the standard reads a scale's limits as -- the limiting values before the conversion is applied. Written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`. Absent, the scale states no limit and the conversion applies to every stored value; it is not the physical range, which is the type's `range`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

fields.name: package
fields.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

element_kinds.description: One named value of a `texttable`: a member of its `entries` collection, never a standalone element, so it has no file and no layer-level address. It has an enum literal's shape.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The entry's identity inside its table, written as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `SHORT-LABEL` and its `VT`, exactly as an enum literal's name; must not be blank, and immutable.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The integer the entry stands for, emitted as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free text about the entry. Written into the generated ARXML as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

element_kinds.description: The limits of a linear computation method's scale, on the stored side. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. Either limit may be left out; the lower one must not be above the upper one, and the two may be equal only when both are closed.

fields.name: lower
fields.description: The lowest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

fields.name: upper
fields.description: The highest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `UPPER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

element_kinds.description: One limit of a scale: a stored value and whether the limit itself belongs to the interval. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The limit's stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float; it accepts neither NaN nor ±Infinity.

fields.name: interval
fields.description: Whether the limit belongs to the interval: `closed` (it does; the default, as an absent `INTERVAL-TYPE` is) or `open` (it does not). Written as the limit's `INTERVAL-TYPE`.

expected.notes: The same document the default form answers with `description` restored on the layer, on every kind and on every field that declares one, and with the three descriptor booleans spelled out where the default form omits them at `false` — `optional` on the layer, `required` and `immutable` on every field. Nothing else is restored, because nothing else is left out. `baseline` is the stand-in token every vector carries; a harness replaces it with the project's own.
